stories.title: Abbas eyes maiden five-wicket haul on home soil as Pakistan prepare for Sri Lanka Tests
summary: Veteran fast bowler Mohammad Abbas is targeting a maiden five-wicket haul on home soil as Pakistan prepare for their two-Test series against Sri Lanka, hoping to add a missing milestone to an otherwise impressive Test career.

Pakistan’s preparations for the series are progressing well, with the opening Test scheduled to be played at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium from November 9 to 13, followed by the second match at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium from November 17 to 21.
Every boy is in match practice, which is very good for Test cricket and for Pakistan,” Abbas said.

stories.title: LPG availability, fair pricing among govt priorities, says petroleum minister
summary: Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Saturday that addressing public concerns over the availability and unfair pricing of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) was a government priority.
According to state-run Radio Pakistan, the minister attended the first meeting of the committee formed to ensure transparent auction of LPG.
Earlier this week, Malik assured the public that the government will make utmost efforts to meet the demand for LPG during the winter months.

stories.title: Bushra Bibi approaches IHC over worsening eyesight, seeks treatment from doctors of her choice
summary: Meanwhile, Barrister Salman Safdar, counsel for the PTI founder, has submitted an affidavit before the IHC detailing his recent meeting with Imran and Bushra at Adiala jail and raising serious concerns about her eyesight.
Barrister Safdar stated that Bushra had specifically requested that her medical examination and treatment be conducted by her personal doctors.

The application urges the IHC to intervene to ensure that Bushra receives immediate specialist medical attention and that her deteriorating eyesight is not further compromised due to any delay in treatment.

stories.title: France braces for protests as Yellow Vests urge ‘mass disobedience’
summary: French unions and student groups are set to take to the streets for another day of protests on Saturday, while the Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris despite a ban by authorities.
Student groups and trade unions have called for an authorised march in central Paris “against the high cost of living and in support of young people”.

Authorities are determined to prevent a repeat of the rioting and looting that marred the Oct 17 demonstrations, although the interior ministry said Thursday’s protests had “generally gone well” despite 642 arrests.

stories.title: Pakistan, Sudan to sign MoU on cybercrime cooperation
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Sudan on Saturday decided to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to enhance cooperation in combating cybercrime, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of Interior.

Briefing the visiting minister, Naqvi said that with Nadra’s cooperation, 36 million citizenship cards, 9 million national identity cards, 18 million birth certificates and 500,000 death certificates had been issued in Sudan.

A day ago, the Sudanese interior minister held a meeting with Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and discussed avenues to enhance bilateral cooperation between their countries.

stories.title: Australia's Khawaja claims entire team knew about 'Sandpapergate'
summary: Usman Khawaja claimed on Saturday that the entire Australian team knew about the 2018 “Sandpapergate” scandal in Cape Town and said they also employed the tactic during the previous Test at Port Elizabeth.

Captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were sent home in disgrace and found by a Cricket Australia investigation to be the only three players with prior knowledge of the ball-tampering plot.

You get to a place where you move on, and I’ve moved on with my life.” In the book, according to the newspaper, Khawaja recounts that discussions about ways to rough up the ball were first held in the dressing room during the second Test at Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha.

stories.title: Democratic victories bring historic breakthroughs for women and minorities
summary: In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor of a US state, while Xavier Becerra was the first Latino elected as governor of California.

Lewis, ​who voted for Wisconsin Democrat David Crowley, the state’s first Black governor-elect, said voters were frustrated with the economic pressures facing their families. “When you start getting into people’s pockets, you have a problem,” Lewis said.
In Florida, US Representative Byron Donalds, ​a Republican, became the first Black governor elected ⁠in the state’s history.

stories.title: Making the most of America’s midterm tsunami
summary: Yet it would be a grave mistake to take a further step by concluding that voters’ overwhelming rejection of Trump and his Republican Party marks a full-throated public re-embrace of democracy.
Voters’ demand for the rule of law and democracy has helped destroy Trump’s MAGA movement.
The Democrats have opportunities, in Congress and also in newly-won state capitals, to show voters they understand that only democracy will be responsive on the economic front.

stories.title: Just like cars, Chinese motorcycles out to conquer Europe
summary: Just as with electric cars, Chinese motorcycle brands are roaring into European markets, with high-performance, cut‑price models starting to make a name for themselves.

In 2025, China became the EU’s second-largest supplier of motorcycles, behind Japan, accounting for 27.1 per cent of imports with sales at one billion euros, according to a report published Thursday by the European Association of Motorcycle Manufacturers (ACEM).

At the CFMoto stand, executives from a major Italian brand stopped by on Wednesday to have a look at the high-speed sport bike. “We’ll have to see its price, but in the long run it could hurt us,” commented one of them, who asked to remain anonymous.

stories.title: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war
summary: Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme.
Reward offered The US military said it was offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme.
Early on Saturday, Iran’s Tasnim news agency reported that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, adding there was no official information about any damage.

stories.title: Pakistan warns UN against weakening peacekeeping amid budget cuts
summary: UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has urged the United Nations not to allow financial constraints and cost-cutting measures to weaken its peacekeeping operations, warning that reductions in resources could undermine the organisation’s ability to maintain international peace and security.
Ambassador Shah’s intervention comes at a time when peacekeeping operations are confronting not only financial difficulties but also increasingly complicated political and security environments.

Pakistan also stressed the importance of the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations, known as C-34, describing it as the universal intergovernmental forum for collectively shaping peacekeeping policy.

stories.title: Rapist of girl sentenced to 32-year imprisonment in Haripur
summary: HARIPUR: A court has sentenced a man after convicting him of raping a mentally challenged minor girl to a total of 32 years in prison.
After a six-year trial, GBV court judge Shah Faisal sentenced the convict to rigorous imprisonment for 25 years and fined him Rs200,000 for rape.
He was also convicted under Section 53 of the Child Protection Act and sentenced to seven years in prison, with an additional fine of Rs100,000.

stories.title: Eight police officials dismissed over negligence in Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: Eight police officials were dismissed from service after a departmental inquiry proved them guilty of negligence in service delivery to citizens and corruption.
He added that the sub-inspector was dismissed for negligence in service delivery to the citizens, while the ASI was sacked for serious negligence in professional duties.
The head constable and two constables were dismissed for negligence in professional duties, while three constables were shown the door on complaints of corruption.

stories.title: 60pc work on development of E-12 complete, says Capital Development Authority
summary: Overall, more than 60 percent of the development work has been completed so far,” read a press release issued by CDA.

It said that on direction of CDA Chairman Sohail Ashraf, development activities were continuing rapidly in E-12 by the relevant departments. “In Sector E-12/4, earthwork has been completed, while work on the base, sub-base and drainage is progressing rapidly.

Meanwhile, in Sector E-12/1, TST has been completed in 25 streets, while earthwork is underway in the remaining streets.” “Completion of development work in Sector E-12 and other sectors is among the top priorities of the CDA administration.

stories.title: Stubble burning: 593 fire hotspots identified in eight districts across Punjab
summary: The incidents were detected in Hafizabad, Sheikhupura, Nankana Sahib, Faisalabad, Kasur, Sialkot, Sargodha and Gujranwala through satellite-based monitoring, field surveillance and specialised night squads, according to the EPA.

The agency has expanded its monitoring mechanism through the Punjab Climate Watch Hub, which analyses satellite-generated fire anomalies round the clock and forwards verified alerts to district field teams for on-ground action.

During the visits, he directed officials to ensure uninterrupted night patrolling, immediate response to satellite alerts and strict monitoring of agricultural areas identified as vulnerable to crop-residue burning.

stories.title: 12 arrested from two illegal call centres in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Friday arrested 12 suspects, including two women, at two illegal call centres.

Preliminary investigations revealed that the call centres were defrauding common people in Canada, the United States and other countries through fraudulent offers of mobile phone upgrades, network packages and SIM deals.
The suspects would impersonate representatives of well-known telecommunications companies to obtain the victims’ financial information and carry out illegal financial transactions and card fraud.

stories.title: Punjab Revenue Authority wants electronic invoice system at all hotels, restaurants
summary: LAHORE: Punjab Revenue Authority (PRA) has sought all hotels and restaurants to be equipped with the electronic invoice monitoring system (EIMS) for timely payment of taxes.
During the meeting, matters concerning installation of EIMS in the hotel industry and tax compliance came under discussion.
The association office-bearers assured the PRA of its full cooperation in initiatives aimed at improving the tax system and promoting digitalisation.

stories.title: Woman found drowned in Karachi three days after disappearance, two daughters still missing
summary: KARACHI: A woman who had been missing with her two minor daughters for the past three days was found dead in a water main near Dumba Goth on Friday, officials said.
Malir Cantonment SHO Agha Abdul Rasheed said the woman’s body was found floating in the main line, which carries water from Keenjhar Lake.

The SHO said there was a farmhouse in the area off the Superhighway, and police were trying to obtain its CCTV footage to establish whether the woman had jumped into the water line along with her daughters or whether someone had thrown them into it.

stories.title: Mayor Murtaza Wahab inaugurates new OPD block at Abbasi Shaheed Hospital in Karachi
summary: Addressing the ceremony, the mayor said that the opening of the new OPD block would provide patients with improved medical facilities, marking another important step towards upgrading healthcare services at ASH along modern lines.
The mayor said that he intended to establish a board titled Friends of Karachi to oversee and improve the affairs of ASH.
The mayor said that in the first phase, the priority was to activate and improve the hospital’s medical services.

stories.title: Doctor shot dead inside clinic in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: A 50-year-old doctor was gunned down inside his clinic in Gulshan-i-Maymar on Friday evening, police said.
A police spokesperson attributed the murder to personal enmity and said further investigations were underway.
Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hasan Lanjar took notice of the doctor’s murder and sought a detailed report from the West SSP.

stories.title: The Pakistan Medical Association seeks forensic audit of disease control programmes
summary: In a statement, the association regretted that Pakistan continued to lag “disastrously” behind global health milestones despite billions of rupees funnelled through international grants, donor funding and national exchequers over the decades.

Chronic institutional inertia, lack of transparency, lack of grassroots execution, and administrative malpractices have rendered these vertical programmes ineffective,” Dr Abdul Ghafoor Shoro of PMA said.

On behalf of the association, he demanded the urgent implementation of independent forensic and financial audits, overseen by credible, non-partisan financial watchdogs, of all federal and provincial disease control programmes and NGOs dealing with polio, TB, HIV and hepatitis.

stories.title: Trump makes hardliner Stephen Miller his chief of staff after midterm defeat
summary: US President Donald Trump named longtime aide Stephen Miller as his chief of staff on Friday, giving the architect of some of his toughest domestic policies one of the most powerful jobs in Washington after Republicans lost control of Congress.
Miller driving immigration crackdown Miller, 41, is one of Trump's longest-serving aides and one of only a few who served throughout his first and second terms in office.

Since Trump's return to the White House in 2025, Miller has officially served as deputy chief of staff under Wiles, but he has wielded outsize influence across much of Trump's domestic agenda and has had the president's ear.

stories.title: KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi slams ‘double standard’ of Fazl
summary: I don’t want to go into the details of why you send the children of poor people to Afghanistan, while your own sons go to Turkiye, Europe and the United States,” he said.
The governor said Fazlur Rahman and his family had themselves stated that they could not leave their homes after evening.
He added that the JUI-F chief had been attacked and his brother intercepted by terrorists.

stories.title: Lampard says hair pull warranted Coventry penalty
summary: Coventry City manager Frank Lampard said a hair pull on Caleb Yirenkyi warranted a penalty as he questioned three refereeing decisions in Friday's 3-1 ​Premier League defeat at Everton.

Lampard was left frustrated as he felt Coventry should have been awarded a ​first-half penalty when James Tarkowski pulled Yirenkyi’s hair while challenging for the ​ball, but referee Stuart Attwell rejected their appeals.
Everton manager David Moyes, whose side climbed to fifth while Coventry remained 16th, rejected the handball claim but also criticised the ⁠hair-pulling ​rule.

stories.title: Peshawar-Lahore direct flight to begin on November 9, says K-P governor
summary: Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Saturday announced that a direct flight between Peshawar and Lahore would begin on November 9, providing air connectivity between the two cities.
Kundi said a direct flight from Peshawar to Quetta had already been launched, while efforts were underway to establish further air links with other parts of the province.

In a separate event, Kundi addressed a ceremony in Peshawar and said the provincial government had been taking steps to improve the healthcare sector, provide facilities to doctors and hospitals, and establish a strong healthcare institution.

stories.title: Nepra raises industrial tariff to Rs25.30 per unit, despite dissent
summary: Interestingly, Nepra Chairman Waseem Mukhtar fully endorsed the written arguments and positions taken by the dissenting members but subsequently exercised his special casting vote to approve the revised rate of Rs25.30 per unit instead of retaining the existing rate of Rs22.98.

The dissenting members argued that compliance with the federal cabinet’s decision and Nepra’s own directives required a reassessment of the existing rate of Rs22.98 per unit to determine whether it should be retained, revised or suspended.
The two members, therefore, recommended the temporary suspension of the tariff package rather than choosing the proposed rate of Rs25.30 or above per unit.

stories.title: Alcaraz reaches Paris Masters semis
summary: Despite only playing one match en route to the quarter-finals, Alcaraz showed no signs of rust as he seized his first break opportunity in the fifth game of the opening set, whipping a forehand passing shot around the stranded Fritz.
A fine passing shot saved a second match point in the next game before Alcaraz wiped out the break and then completed his Houdini act by breaking Fritz again to set up a decider.

Alcaraz still had to save break points in a match that always threatened another twist but, as it rumbled towards a conclusion, he brought up two match points on his own serve, sealing the first with a powerful forehand that Fritz could only get a frame on.

stories.title: Bushra Bibi's eyes in 'extremely vulnerable condition', Barrister Safdar tells IHC
summary: Earlier this week, government authorities allowed Safdar to meet Imran and Bushra at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail after a gap of several months.
In the affidavit submitted today, Safdar stated that Adiala jail authorities informed him on October 31 that his meeting with Imran and Bushra had been scheduled for 3:30pm on November 2.

According to Safdar, Bushra was wearing unusually dark black glasses during the meeting and when she removed them at his request and that of the PTI founder, she appeared to be in severe distress, he stated.

stories.title: Polls close in New Zealand's general election as vote counting begins
summary: Polling stations across New Zealand closed on Saturday in the country's general election to elect a new government, according to media reports.
Polling stations opened at 9am (2000GMT Friday) and closed at 7pm (0600GMT Saturday).
Vote counting began after polls closed, according to Radio New Zealand.

stories.title: Pakistani astronaut to join China space station's Shenzhou-24 mission
summary: A Pakistani astronaut will join China's space station on ​this year's Shenzhou-24 mission, as part of ‌bilateral cooperation under Beijing's Belt and Road Initiative, Chinese state media reported on Saturday.
The ​first foreign visitor to the ​space station will participate as a payload ⁠specialist in the mission, broadcaster ​CCTV reported, citing the China Manned Space ​Agency.
Read: Pakistan to launch first astronaut into space from China on Nov 25: Ahsan Iqbal Beijing has not announced the date of the mission.

stories.title: Delhi world's most polluted major city on eve of Diwali, Swiss group says
summary: India has ordered schools in and around Delhi to offer online classes, and encouraged people to work from home ahead of Diwali on Sunday, which is usually marked by the widespread use of firecrackers that further worsen the air quality.
IQAir ranked Delhi first among the world's major cities at 10:35am (0505 GMT), with a US air quality index reading of 581, double that of Lahore in neighbouring Pakistan, at 285.
Read: Diwali celebrations light up the city sky India's Central Pollution Control Board put Delhi's air quality index at 363 at 10am, in the "very poor" category.

stories.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi cruise missile over Riyadh
summary: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Saturday that its air defences intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia's Riyadh region.

Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Houthis since 2015, after the group seized the capital, Sanaa and other parts of the country the previous year.
The army said the Houthis suffered heavy losses in personnel and equipment, while government forces were consolidating positions in recaptured areas and clearing mines.

stories.title: California voters reject billionaire wealth tax proposal
summary: Voters in the state of California rejected a ballot measure that would have taxed the wealth of billionaire residents, a first in the US, according to a projection by the Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ).
The measure would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on billionaires’ wealth, with most revenue going to state healthcare programs and the rest to food assistance and education.
The state Democratic Party, the American Federation of Labor, the Congress of Industrial Organisations and the Teamsters unions supported the measure, while California Gov. Gavin Newsom opposed it.

stories.title: Qatar says its mediation efforts between US and Iran continue to prevent escalation
summary: US offers up to $20m reward for information on Iran's nuclear program: CENTCOM The US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) said on Friday that the Rewards for Justice program is offering up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear program.

Trump says US "could be an occupier" in Iran US President Donald Trump on Friday suggested that Washington "could be an occupier" in Iran, claiming it controls the Strait of Hormuz and is extracting record amounts of oil from the strategic waterway.

"We’re taking out more oil now than we have at any time in the history of the Hormuz Strait." Asked whether US forces carried out reported strikes near Iran's Qeshm Island on Friday, Trump initially declined to discuss it but acknowledged limited military operations.

stories.title: Thousands took to streets to celebrate PTI govt’s ouster: Muqam
summary: The minister said that despite remaining in power in the province for nearly 13 and a half years, the PTI had failed to address the basic problems of the people or put the province on the path of development.

Paying tribute to the armed forces, the minister said the Pakistan Army was not only guarding the country’s borders but also standing shoulder to shoulder with the nation in every difficult situation.

He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan had achieved significant successes on the defence, diplomatic and economic fronts.

stories.title: KP to introduce mobile drug testing labs
summary: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will introduce five advanced mobile drug screening laboratories next week to strengthen the monitoring of medicines and detect substandard, counterfeit and suspicious drugs in markets across the province.
The vans will be deployed across different divisions of the province, enabling drug inspectors to examine medicines in markets and other locations.

If the initial screening identifies suspicious or substandard medicines, inspectors will collect samples and send them to the Drug Testing Laboratory in Peshawar for detailed analysis and further action.

stories.title: PHC grants interim relief to employees in suspension, transfer cases
summary: BANNU: The Peshawar High Court’s Bannu Bench has granted interim relief in two cases challenging provincial departments’ powers to transfer, post, and suspend employees following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The bench suspended the orders concerning the suspension of the Bannu regional municipal officer (RMO) and the transfer of an assistant director of the local government and rural development department, ruling that the status quo be maintained in both cases.

However, he argued that despite these provisions, the secretary local government suspended RMO Baloch on Oct 30, while the local government and rural development department’s director general transferred assistant director Inamullah to the directorate general on Oct 15.

stories.title: RCCI, Wasa discuss water shortage, urban flooding in Pindi
summary: During the meeting, the Wasa managing director gave a comprehensive presentation outlining the authority’s operational capacity, development projects, future water requirements and strategies for improving municipal services.

The Asian Development Bank-funded Dreams-I project, worth approximately US$225 million, is also supporting water supply improvements, infrastructure expansion and solarisation initiatives in Rawalpindi.

Wasa officials further briefed participants on ongoing Punjab Development Programme projects involving replacement of 106 kilometres of old water supply lines, installation of tube wells, construction of reservoirs and development of sewerage and drainage infrastructure.

stories.title: New state lounge planned at Islamabad airport ahead of SCO summit
summary: RAWALPINDI: The Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) has initiated construction of a new State Lounge at Islamabad International Airport as part of Pakistan’s preparations for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit scheduled to be hosted in Islamabad in August 2027.
The new State Lounge forms part of Pakistan’s preparations for the SCO Summit, scheduled to be hosted in Islamabad in August 2027.
Meanwhile, Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) management has started deep cleaning its fleet of aircraft in an effort to significantly improve cabin maintenance and aircraft cleanliness.

stories.title: US stamps case: suspects’ family members get bail
summary: LAHORE: A sessions court on Friday granted interim pre-arrest bail to three family members of the suspects in an alleged online sale of fake US postage stamps worth $126m.
The applicants, Wasim Akram, Ayesha Akram and Sameera Anjum, who were declared co-suspects in the case along with key suspects appeared before the court for the bail.
Regarding the key suspects, Faheem and Naeem Akram, the defence counsel argued that the prosecution had so far failed to collect any concrete evidence against them.
